competitors.title: Trigger.dev AI Agents Overview
key_points: chat.agent() runs conversations as single long-lived durable tasks — resumes across refreshes, deploys, and crashes
Native AI SDK support — text, tool calls, reasoning, custom data parts all flow through useChat over custom ChatTransport
Multi-turn conversations with server-side state accumulation — clients only ship new messages
Production primitives: stop generation, steering, edits, branching, sub-agents, HITL tool approvals, version upgrades, recovery from cancel/crash/OOM
Every turn is a span in Trigger.dev dashboard; sessions queryable via sessions.list for inbox-style UIs

competitors.title: Trigger.dev Human-in-the-Loop Pattern
key_points: HITL built with tools that have no execute() function — streamText ends with tool call pending when LLM calls it
Turn flow: User message → run() → LLM calls askUser (no execute) → streamText ends → frontend renders UI → user responds via addToolOutput → next turn resumes with answer merged
Frontend uses sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithToolCalls to auto-fire next turn after user answers
Detect paused turns via finishReason === 'tool-calls' in onTurnComplete
chat.history.getPendingToolCalls() returns pending HITL tool calls for gating actions like regenerate
Two persistence patterns: overwrite every turn (simplest, just store latest uiMessages) or checkpoint nodes (immutable history per pause)
Multi-pause turns supported — each pause fires own onTurnComplete, only last firing has finishReason === 'stop'

competitors.title: Trigger.dev Wait for Token (Waitpoint Tokens API)
key_points: Waitpoint tokens pause task runs until externally completed — used for approval workflows and HITL processes
wait.createToken() creates token with optional timeout (default 10m), returns id + url + publicAccessToken
wait.forToken() blocks task execution until token completed, returns Result object with ok/output or error
wait.completeToken() completes token with arbitrary output data
publicAccessToken for client-side completion via CORS-enabled endpoint (no backend proxy needed)
HTTP callback support: POST to token.url to complete token from external services like Replicate webhooks
IdempotencyKey and TTL support to prevent duplicate completions

competitors.title: Trigger.dev Frontend: Tool Approvals and Actions
key_points: needsApproval: true on tool definitions pauses execution until user approves/denies via frontend
addToolApprovalResponse() for Approve/Deny buttons in chat UI
sendAutomaticallyWhen: lastAssistantMessageIsCompleteWithApprovalResponses to auto-resume after approval
Custom actions (undo, rollback, edit) via transport.sendAction() — wake agent but don't fire new turn
Actions fire only hydrateMessages and onAction — not onTurnStart/run/onTurnComplete
Gating: refuse regenerate while HITL tool call is pending using getPendingToolCalls()

competitors.title: Trigger.dev v4 Beta Launch — Waitpoints and HITL Tokens
key_points: Waitpoints are new v4 primitive that block runs until conditions met — power all wait functions
Single waitpoint can block multiple runs; single run can be blocked by multiple waitpoints
HITL tokens: wait.createToken with timeout, pass token to task via trigger payload, wait.forToken in task
Dashboard: manual complete/skip/timeout for waitpoints, useful for testing
Self-hosted workers and Kubernetes support available for production deployment
Idempotency for triggerAndWait and batchTriggerAndWait — cache results across runs

competitors.title: Trigger.dev Sub-Agents Pattern
key_points: Parent agent delegates to sub-agent via async generator tool pattern (async function*)
AgentChat.sendMessage() to sub-agent, yield* stream.messages() streams UIMessage snapshots to frontend
toModelOutput compresses full sub-agent output for parent LLM token efficiency
Multi-turn sub-agent: Map of conversationId → AgentChat persists across parent turns via snapshot
Cleanup via explicit close, idle timeout, or suspend timeout — no leaked resources
Frontend sees sub-agent work building up inside parent's tool call card

angles: Two distinct HITL patterns: Waitpoint tokens (task-level pause for approval) vs chat agent tool approvals (turn-level pause for user input during AI conversation)
Wait.forToken is the general-purpose HITL primitive — works in any task regardless of AI chat — complete from browser, backend, or HTTP callback
Chat agent HITL via no-execute tools is specific to conversational AI with useChat frontend — auto-resumes with sendAutomaticallyWhen
Trigger.dev vs Inngest vs Temporal: Trigger.dev's waitpoint-based HITL is unique among serverless task runners for AI agent approval workflows
Multi-pause turns: a single logical turn can pause multiple times — each pause fires its own onTurnComplete with finishReason === 'tool-calls'
Checkpoint vs overwrite persistence choice: overwrite is simplest for basic HITL; checkpoint nodes provide immutable audit trail for compliance-heavy apps
Sub-agent + HITL combination: parent agent delegates to sub-agent with toModelOutput compression, while keeping parent-level HITL gates for final approval
Gating actions during HITL pause: use chat.history.getPendingToolCalls() to block regenerate/undo while tool call is awaiting approval
Self-hosting option: Trigger.dev v4 supports Docker and Kubernetes self-hosting, critical for enterprises needing HITL compliance on private infrastructure
Growing ecosystem: Trigger.dev powers Cal.com, MagicSchool AI, Midday, Capy — all using durable HITL workflows for AI agent production systems
